say: Her feet used to slide along the ledge while she walked.
Her legs swung back and forth on a timer, while her body moved along at a constant speed, so the two never matched.
Now, instead of animating her legs, the walk decides where each foot is planted, and the legs follow.
The walk follows the timing of a real human step. The heel strikes the ground, the foot lies flat, the heel lifts, and the toe pushes off, before the leg swings forward.
A planted foot stays at a fixed point on the ledge. The hips keep moving, and each leg is bent so that it reaches its foot.
When she turned around, she used to spin on the spot, and her feet slid almost ten centimetres.
Now she turns in three steps, and each foot stays where it lands.
Whether she is walking, turning, kicking or sitting down, her feet now slip by less than a millimetre.
